summary: Folke Bergman worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Uppsala University (~1920–1924) and served as Amanuens of East Asian collections at the Museum of Far Eastern Antiquities (~1935–1946).

Forbes Falconer studied Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological subjects. He attended Marischal College and the University of Aberdeen (~1820–1826) and studied under Silvestre de Sacy, Garcin de Tassy, and Heinrich Ewald. In 1834, he became Professor at University College London.

Forster Fitzgerald Arbuthnot worked in Indology. He studied at the East India Company College (1851) and served in the Indian Civil Service from 1853 to 1878, where he was Collector of Bombay City and Island.

Frances Wood works in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Newnham College, Cambridge, and Peking University. Her posts include the British Library (~1977–2013) and North Bristol NHS Trust as a clinical psychologist (2023).
Francesca Fremantle specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS University of London and studied under Chögyam Trungpa (~1971–1987).

Francesca Tarocco works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London in 2005. She served as Professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (2016) and Visiting Associate Professor at NYU Shanghai (2017).

Francesco Adolfo Cannizzaro worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He studied under Angelo De Gubernatis (~1891–1893) and earned a law degree from the University of Catania by 1894.

Francesco Cimmino studied Indology at the University of Naples under Michele Kerbaker and at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia. He taught at Liceo Antonio Genovesi and served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Naples (1914–1935).

Francesco Lorenzo Pullè, an Indologist and linguist, studied under Angelo De Gubernatis, Albrecht Weber, Theodor Mommsen, and Heinrich Kiepert. He was a professor at the University of Padua (1875–1889), University of Pisa (1889–1899), and University of Bologna (1899–1925).

Francesco Ribezzo worked in linguistics and archaeology. He studied at Naples under Michele Kerbaker, Leipzig, and under Alfredo Trombetti. He held docentships at Naples (1914–1921) and Messina (1921–1925), and was Professor at the University of Palermo (1925–1948).

Francesco Scerbo worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Seminario Vescovile di Nicastro and under Angelo De Gubernatis and Antelmo Severini. At the University of Florence, he was libero docente (1892) and incaricato for Hebrew (1903–1924).

Francesco Sferra specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, having studied under Raffaele Torella (~1990–1999). He held positions at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2002–~2005) and University of Naples Federico II (attested 2010–2016).

Linguist Francis A. Wood studied at Northwestern, Göttingen, and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. ~1895). He held professorships at Chaddock College (1890–1893) and Cornell College (1897–1903), and was an Assistant Professor at the University of Chicago (1903–1927).

Francis Balfour worked in Indology and medicine, completing his Dr.Med. at the University of Edinburgh by 1767. He served in the East India Company as Assistant Surgeon (1769) and full surgeon (1777–1807).

Francis Brandt worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned a B.A. from Brasenose College, Oxford (~1858–1870), served in the Indian Civil Service (~1862–1889), and lectured in Tamil and Indian Law at the University of Cambridge (1891–1895).
Francis Brinkley worked in Japanology. He attended the Royal School Dungannon and later held a post at the University of Tokyo (~1878–1881).

Francis Buchanan-Hamilton studied medicine at Edinburgh under John Hope (M.D. ~1783). He served in the Bengal Medical Service (1794–1815), directed the Indian Botanic Garden (1814–1815), and became Keeper of the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh (1815–1829).

Francis Gladwin worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He was a founding member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1812) and was appointed the first Professor of Persian at Fort William College in 1801.

Francis Harold Cook specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy, completing doctoral requirements at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1970). He was a professor at the University of California, Riverside (~1970–1989), and chaired the Numata Center in 1999.
Francis John Monahan worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Balliol College, Oxford, in 1883 and entered the Indian Civil Service as a civil servant in 1885.
